Utilization and past delinquencies interact strongly: the effect of utilization is much larger for applicants with two delinquencies than for those with none, and the effect of delinquencies is also much larger at high utilization, so the two should be read together rather than separately.

Income and credit history length each matter moderately, with higher income and longer history associated with lower predicted risk, and a longer history also weakens the risk added by recent credit inquiries.
The debt-to-income ratio and recent credit inquiries have small effects, with higher debt-to-income and more inquiries nudging risk upward.
Age, feature_a and feature_b have effects too small to resolve at this sample size, so the data do not show that they affect predicted default.
